newsitem.title: FRANCE: France sees millennium as time for dreams.
newsitem.headline: France sees millennium as time for dreams.

text.p: French Prime Minister Alain Juppe kicked off preparations on Thursday for a nationwide celebration to usher in the new millennium, calling it a time with "a fantastic potential for dreams".
Juppe told a news conference he wanted France's passage into the 21st century to be marked by joy and hope, "making it first of all a moment of festivity but also of reflection and taking stock".

The official countdown to new year's eve 1999 will begin this Saturday night when the mayor of Paris throws a switch lighting a sign erected on the Eiffel Tower that will count down the 1,000 days to the special night.

Juppe said preparations would include an advertising campaign, launched on Thursday evening, including the slogan "1,000 days to create the year 2000", aimed at creating excitement ahead of the celebrations.

Several large festivals will be organised in French cities over the next three years. The national committee organising the celebration will randomly select 20,000 French people who will celebrate their 20th birthday in the year 2000 for all-expenses-paid trips to destinations around the world.
On December 31, 2000 -- considered by many the true start to the third millenium -- France plans an around-the-world sailing race starting in the port of Brest.
Juppe said he wants France's commemoration of the start of the next century to be an honourable memory for the country.

"It would give me great satisfaction if future generations remembered us as men and women who were generous, committed, confident in the future of humanity and resolute in the pursuit of progress and justice," Juppe said.
